info.title: EthniAfrica API v2 - AFRIK
info.description:
API publique v2 basée sur la méthodologie AFRIK. Identifiants stables (FLG_*, PPL_*, codes ISO 3166-1 alpha-3) et format de réponse standardisé avec pagination. Cette API fournit un accès structuré aux données ethnographiques et linguistiques de l'Afrique.

## Authentication and rate limits

No key is required. A request without an `Authorization` header is served on the **anonymous** tier, metered at 60 requests per minute per client IP.

An API key passed as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` selects a larger quota: `public` keys 600 requests per minute, `partner` keys 6,000, `admin` keys unmetered. A key that is present but unknown, revoked or expired is refused with `401 invalid_api_key` rather than served anonymously, so a broken integration fails loudly instead of silently dropping to the anonymous quota.

Metered responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; an exhausted quota answers `429` with `Retry-After`. The figures above are the deployment defaults. The `/api/v2/keys` self-service endpoints are the exception to all of this: they authenticate a signed-in contributor's session instead.

## Response envelope

Every `/api/v2/*` response uses the Module #0 envelope: `{ data, meta: { license, attribution, pagination?, confidence?, pinned_url?, translation? }, errors }`. License and attribution are always present (AR8); `errors` is empty on success and populated on non-2xx responses. List endpoints place their pagination values under `meta.pagination`.

## French only (breaking)

The site publishes French alone, so the locale parameters that selected English are narrowed to `fr`: `lang` on `GET /api/v2/search` and `GET /api/v2/search/companions`, and `language` in the `POST /api/v2/flags` body. `lang=en` is now refused with 400 on the two searches; an unknown flag `language` still fails closed to French. Search no longer matches English names; the `nameEn` / `languageFamilyNameEn` fields keep their shape and still carry the value in the record. `contentLanguage` in companion payloads is always `fr`.

## 2.3.0 — translated records (additive)

The five single-entity endpoints accept `?lang=fr|en`. `fr` is the authored language and the default; `en` overlays the translation record when one exists and declares how it was produced in `meta.translation` — `human`, `machine_reviewed` or `machine` — with `stale: true` when the French moved on a field the reader is shown since it was translated. Fields whose subject is a word are withheld at `machine` provenance and served in French until a human has reviewed them (REQ-142, REQ-143). Lists, facets and search stay authored-French. Retired since: the data is no longer translated, `?lang` is ignored and every record is served as authored.

## 2.1.0 — one source-tier vocabulary (breaking)

Source authority is now one three-value scale — `official` | `referenced` | `unverified` — spoken identically by the database, the payloads and the UI. Provenance stays on the separate `source_kind` axis, so AI-generated text is `tier: "unverified"` + `source_kind: "ai_generated"` rather than a tier of its own.

Removed, all superseded by `tier`:

- the numeric evidence-tier property on `Source`, `ReferenceSource` and `ReferenceCreateInput` (a `1 | 2 | null` scale that could not express an unverified source);
- the legacy `Source.type` enum, which read a column dropped in migration 015 and was therefore always `null`;
- the two catalogue gating properties on `Source.policy`, which decided whether a citation could be published at all. Under the source doctrine no citation is refused, so `Source.policy.tier` carries the signal instead.

get.summary: Search the main corpus or the dedicated quiz lens
get.description: Full-text search, ranked in Postgres by `afrik_search_peoples` / `afrik_search_countries` (migration 052): an accent-insensitive exact name match first, then `ts_rank` over the weighted `search_vector` (migration 043: A = name and autonym, B = exonyms, C/D = prose) OR the accent-insensitive `name_unaccent_vector`, both queried with the `:*` prefix operator on the last word of `q` — so a partial trailing word ("bamba") matches a longer indexed name ("Bambara"), and an unaccented query ("mande") matches an accented name ("Mandé") by construction, not by stemmer coincidence (REQ-129). Relevance is multiplied for peoples by a 0.5–1.0 confidence factor. Language families rank in SQL too (migration 068): exact > prefix > substring on the folded name, then a tier for a match found only in their decolonial prose. `q` no longer accepts websearch syntax — quoted phrases, `OR` and `-` exclusions are not recognised (DEC-034); each word except the last must now match as a complete word. Each result carries `relevance`, `exactMatch` and a `snippet` whose matched terms are wrapped in `[[` and `]]` — deliberately not HTML, because `ts_headline` does not escape the source document. `relevance` is comparable within an array and not between arrays. Each entity kind is returned in its own array, and `results` carries the same hits merged into one cross-kind ranking on `normalizedScore` (migration 068) — the magnitude that, unlike `relevance`, is comparable between kinds. Without `lens`, quiz questions are not queried or returned in the main search stream; with `lens=quiz`, only quiz questions are queried and returned (REQ-121). The dedicated quiz projection contains the stem only: options, the correct answer and the explanation are never returned. Named persons (migration 065, REQ-126) and names (patronymes — migration 066, REQ-135) rank the same way, with patronymes additionally folding in a dmetaphone phonetic match so a misspelling like "Keyta" still reaches the canonical "Keïta" — offered only when nothing answers the query exactly (migration 108, REQ-201). Both fall back to pg_trgm typo tolerance ahead of a no-match. Languages (migration 068, REQ-136) rank the same prefix/accent-insensitive way, with an exact-match bonus that also fires on the ISO 639-3 id — a reader who types "swa" reaches Swahili exactly as precisely as one who types its name. When `total` is 0, `leads` (REQ-125) carries up to 3 near-miss suggestions across peoples, countries, language families and family names — a trigram similarity scan (migrations 094, 110, 111) below the main search's own fuzzy floor, so the reader sees what the engine almost understood instead of a bare empty result. When `total` is greater than 0, `leads` carries only family names offered as a spelling of the searched name (DEC-075): nothing answers the query exactly, the name begins with the query's first letter, and its similarity reaches 0.4. A search scoped with `familyId` or `countryId` never gets a family-name lead, and neither does a query that spells exactly a family name the search found, through its filed name or a recorded spelling, or that a fiche the search found writes as a word in its own text. Each lead names `matchedForm`, the form that scored: a people is scored only on the pieces of its name fields that are one name, a family name on its filed name and its recorded spellings that are one name. The search is served in French. Rate-limited per AR11 (IP: 60 RPM, public key: 600 RPM, partner key: 6 000 RPM).

get.summary: Compose a quiz session for one entity scope
get.description: Draws `count` (5–10, default 8) active questions from the scope named by `pays`, `famille` or `mode`, ordered by the games charter's difficulty ladder — the subject's population decile inside that scope, two easy rounds, four middling, two hard. `mode=aleatoire` is the one track that skips the ladder. Every question is re-validated at serve time against current confidence, human-audit and source-tier state (FR65 gate), so a question that has decayed since the last generation sweep never reaches a player. The answer key ships in the payload (`correctOption`, `explanationFr`, `source`): reveal is client-side, there is nothing to cheat for (no leaderboard, no persistence, no stakes). A track whose pool cannot fill the session asked for answers 422: a short session is a track with no top rung, which the ladder above is the whole point of. A pool that was big enough and was then thinned by the FR65 gate still answers 200, with however many questions survived — including none, the calm empty state.

post.summary: Issue a public read-only API key
post.description:
Issues a shared, IP-bound, read-only public API key.
One key per IP address — returns 409 if a key already exists for this IP.
The address is the one the reverse proxy observed, never a value the
caller supplies in X-Forwarded-For.
Attempts are limited per address (5 an hour), separately from the
anonymous per-minute quota.
Public keys are rate-limited and can only perform read operations.
Partner and admin keys must be requested via the admin UI.
No authentication required for this endpoint. POST only: a GET that
creates a key can be triggered by a crawler, a link preview or a
cross-site request, so the former GET alias was removed.

SearchNamingOriginFactV2.description: Structured origin facts retained only when safe for the reader-facing search surface.

SearchNamingEvidenceSourceV2.description: A hydrated source for a naming assertion. Source identifiers without these details are not exposed as evidence.

SearchNamingEvidenceV2.description: Complete evidence for one naming assertion: the assertion and every resolved cited source travel together.

SearchNamingProjectionV2.description: The server-built naming projection shared by peoples, countries, language families, names and languages in search results.

SearchAnswerV2.description: The six-block answer for one search row. An optional block whose source the fiche leaves empty is omitted, never returned empty. Text comes from the fiche (`lead`, `question`, accounts); where the fiche writes none, the client composes the sentence from `next.template` and its params. next.description: Either the fiche's own question, or the name of a template and its parameters.

count.description: Distinct sources across every account's evidence.

SearchResponseData.description: Search result data for one of two exclusive modes. Without `lens`, `results` is the canonical cross-kind ranking for the five mergeable non-quiz kinds: every hit, best first, each row carrying a `kind` discriminator; languages remain a grouped facet, and quiz questions are neither queried nor returned. With `lens=quiz`, only quiz questions are queried and returned, in both `quizzes` and `results`, while every non-quiz array and total is empty or zero. In the main stream, each entity kind is ALSO returned in its own array, already ordered — an exact name match first (accent- and case-insensitive), then ts_rank over the weighted search_vector (migration 043: A = name and autonym, B = exonyms, C/D = prose) OR the accent-insensitive name_unaccent_vector, both matched with a prefix operator on the last word of q (migration 052, REQ-129), multiplied for peoples by a 0.5–1.0 confidence factor. `relevance` is comparable within an array and NOT between arrays: peoples are scored ts_rank × confidence, countries by bare ts_rank, families by a match tier, persons and patronymes by the same prefix/unaccent/trigram ranking as peoples but with no confidence factor (migration 065, REQ-126; migration 066, REQ-135 — patronymes additionally fold in a dmetaphone phonetic match, withheld when the query has an exact answer: migration 108, REQ-201), languages by the same prefix/unaccent ranking with no confidence factor and an exact-match bonus that also fires on the ISO 639-3 id (migration 068, REQ-136). `normalizedScore` is the magnitude that IS comparable across kinds: migration 069 places each kind's raw relevance inside a band chosen by the match class (exact [0.90,1.00], lexical [0.50,0.90], fallback [0.00,0.50]), and it is what `results` sorts on; languages are exposed as a facet only and are not folded into `results`. A result hit may carry `recordedIn`, field paths and their text where its fiche writes the query as a whole word; source notes do not count. A person's link to a studied people is carried by `peopleLinks[].relationLabel` (`membership` | `observation`) and is never confused with that people's own membership.

peoples.description: Matching peoples, ranked. An exact answer is the filed name or any name the fiche's history tells, compared on afrik_name_key (migration 109). Each carries relevance, exactMatch, normalizedScore, confidence, languageFamilyName, languageFamilyNameEn (migration 084; null when the family has no English name), historyNames and a snippet whose matched terms are wrapped in [[ ]].

countries.description: Matching countries, ranked by ts_rank with name_fr outranking etymology. exactMatch also fires on any name the country's history tells (migration 109). Each carries nameEn beside nameFr, relevance, exactMatch, normalizedScore, historyNames and a snippet. Empty when the request carries only a relation scope.

families.description: Matching language families, ranked by afrik_search_language_families (migration 069): accent-insensitive exact (1.0) > prefix (0.6) > substring (0.3) on name_fr — then a prose tier (0.1) through search_vector for a term that appears only in the decolonial text (DEC-028). exactMatch also fires on any name the family's history tells (migration 109). Each carries nameEn beside nameFr, relevance, exactMatch, normalizedScore, historyNames and a snippet.

persons.description: Matching named persons (REQ-126), ranked by afrik_search_persons (migration 065): exact full_name match, then a prefix/accent-insensitive lexical match, then a pg_trgm typo-tolerance fallback. Each carries relevance, exactMatch, normalizedScore, a snippet, and peopleLinks typing its relation to any studied/belonged-to people.

patronymes.description: Matching names (REQ-135), ranked by afrik_search_patronymes (migration 066): exact name match, then a prefix/accent-insensitive lexical match, then a dmetaphone phonetic match, then a pg_trgm typo-tolerance fallback. A name reached only through its phonetic key is left out of this array, of patronymesTotal and of total when the query has an exact answer in any kind or in the production ledger (migration 108, REQ-201), and when the response offers a family-name lead beside its results, which stands for the spelling the phonetic key was bridging (DEC-075); a name the history tells is an exact answer too (migration 109). Each carries relevance, exactMatch, normalizedScore, historyNames and a snippet.

quizzes.description: Dedicated quiz-lens page: empty without `lens` and populated only with `lens=quiz` (REQ-121). Matches active-bank questions ranked by afrik_search_quiz (migration 069) on the stem, the stimulus, the explanation and the subject entity's name. Revoked questions are invisible; the options, the correct answer and the explanation are never returned.

results.description: Canonical page for the selected mode, ordered on normalizedScore descending, ties broken on the name collated in French then on the id. A hit carries optional recordedIn field paths and text when its fiche writes the query as a whole word; source notes are excluded. Without `lens`, it merges the main stream and excludes quiz questions; with `lens=quiz`, it contains only quiz questions.

languages.description: Matching languages (REQ-136), ranked by afrik_search_languages (migration 068): exact match on the ISO 639-3 id, the name or any name the language's history tells (migration 109), then a prefix/accent-insensitive lexical match. Each carries nameEn, familyName, familyNameEn, relevance, exactMatch, historyNames and a snippet.

peoplesTotal.description: Total people matching the query, not the number returned on this page

familiesTotal.description: Total language families matching the query

personsTotal.description: Total named people matching the query

patronymesTotal.description: Total family names matching the query

quizzesTotal.description: Zero without `lens`; the total number of matching active quiz questions with `lens=quiz`.

places.description: Matching places (REQ-196), ranked by afrik_search_places (migration 100) on the filed name and every nameHistory name. A grouped facet like languages: not folded into `results`.

placesTotal.description: Places matching across every page, not only this one

words.description: Matching word fiches (REQ-196), ranked by afrik_search_words (migration 104) on the filed name and every nameHistory name. Each row carries the six-block `answer` of kind `word`, read from its nameHistory. A grouped facet like places: not folded into `results`.

wordsTotal.description: Word fiches matching across every page, not only this one

total.description: Without `lens`, the sum of the eight non-quiz counts, each across every page. With `lens=quiz`, this equals `quizzesTotal`. Changed in 2.2.0: this used to report the size of the returned page, which made it useless for paging.

leads.description: Near-miss leads (REQ-125), ranked by pg_trgm similarity alone (migrations 094, 110). When total is 0: up to 3 suggestions across peoples, countries, language families and family names. A family name is also offered as a spelling of the searched name when total is greater than 0 (DEC-075): up to 3 family names, only when nothing answers the query exactly (no hit of any kind with exactMatch, no published word, and, once the search has found family names, no family name the query spells exactly through its filed name or a recorded spelling), only when no fiche the search found writes the query as a word in its own text (a clan or name list, a source note: the spelling is then recorded, not a misspelling), only when the family name or one of its recorded spellings begins with the query's first letter (both folded: lower case, accents and apostrophes removed), and only at similarity >= 0.4. A search scoped with familyId or countryId never gets a family-name lead. Empty otherwise, for a multi-name widening and for quiz-lens searches.

nearNames.description: Qualified similar names (REQ-180) for a non-empty search: up to 3 distinct peoples, countries or language families, ranked by pg_trgm similarity and excluding entities already returned by the search. Never a family name (DEC-075). Always empty for zero-result and quiz-lens searches.

nameAnswers.description: Reviewed, sourced answers to « where does this name come from? » for the searched term (REQ-178), matched on the whole term with accents and case ignored and localized by `lang`. Resolved from the term alone, so a search with no hit can still carry one. Empty for a name nobody has reviewed and for quiz-lens searches.

wordAnswers.description: The answer to a published word (REQ-184), read from the production registry and matched on the whole term with accents and case ignored. Carried by the envelope and not by a row, because a word answers to no fiche and may come back with no result at all. Empty for a word nobody published and for quiz-lens searches.

nameSuggestions.description: Reviewed terms a near spelling may have meant (REQ-125), offered only when `total` is 0: within one edit of the searched term, two from eight letters, and never under four letters. The query is never rewritten; a client presents these as choices. Empty otherwise.

NameAnswerV2.description: A reviewed answer to where a name comes from. Written by an editor, never generated per request: rival accounts stay two accounts.

subjects.description: The fiches this answer is about. Several for a term shared by a collective and its parts; shared spelling does not assert that they are related.

uncertainty.description: What the sources leave unsettled, when anything.

sources.description: One entry per key claim: the statement and the sources behind it, in the shape the source-chain sheet reads.

WordAnswerV2.description: The answer to a published word (REQ-184), built from its record in the production registry. It follows the answer contract of the result page (`kind` is always `word`) and lists the queries that find it. A block with no data is an absent key.

queries.description: The accent-free, lowercase queries the registry files for this word.

lead.description: Written in the registry's `answer.lead`; absent when none was written.

names.description: The word's forms, none marked as the one a people gives itself.

path.description: The form of the word in each language it passed through.

SearchLeadV2.description: A near-miss lead (REQ-125): what the search engine almost understood. A people, country or family lead is returned only when the main search's total is 0; a family-name lead is a spelling of the searched name and may come beside results (DEC-075).

kind.description: The entity kind this lead belongs to. `patronyme` is a family name, offered under its filed name.

matchedForm.description: The form that scored (migrations 110 and 111). For a people, a piece of its filed name, its self-appellation or an exonym that is one name: each field is cut at « , », « ; », « ou » and a slash between spaces, never inside a bracket nor at a slash inside a word (« Hai//om » writes a click), and each piece loses its trailing bracket. A piece is one name when it has three words at most, made of letters, accents, hyphens, apostrophes and click marks, and opens on a capital, a letter with no case (ǂHoan), click marks before a letter (« !Kung »), a class prefix before a capital (« amaXhosa ») or a class prefix of one or two lower-case letters joined by a hyphen to a lower-case one (« a-liyan »). Any other piece, such as « pl. Abaganda) », is never scored; « Baganda / Ganda » gives Baganda and Ganda. For a family name, its filed name as filed, or a recorded spelling that is one name: « jarra » reaches Diarra through its spelling Jara. For a country or a language family, its name as filed. Optional: absent from a database without migration 110.

similarity.description: pg_trgm similarity of the folded query against matchedForm, the form that scored: in [0.2, 1] for a people, country or family, in [0.4, 1] for a family name.

SearchNearNameV2.description: A name qualified by the API as similar to a non-empty search, with its pg_trgm similarity. It is a distinct entity from every returned people, country and language-family result.

QuizSearchResultV2.description: A quiz-bank search hit (REQ-121). The projection is a closed list: options_fr and correct_option are the answer key and explanation_fr states the answer in prose, so all three are searched and none is returned — finding a question through search must not answer it.

subjectName.description: French name of the people or country the question is about — how a reader reaches the bank, since nobody searches the wording of a question.

exactMatch.description: True when the reader named the question's subject, not when they retyped the stem.

normalizedScore.description: Cross-kind ranking score on [0,1] (migration 069), the magnitude `results` sorts on.

snippet.description: Match excerpt over the subject, the stem and the stimulus only; matched terms are wrapped in [[ ]]. Never draws on the explanation.

SearchHistoryNamesV2.description: Search rows only (migration 109, REQ-135): every name the fiche's history tells (nameHistory.names[].nameText), in history order and spelt as the fiche writes it. The row answers the query exactly when any of them, folded by afrik_name_key, equals the folded query. An empty array when the fiche has no history block.

SearchHitV2.description: One row of the canonical cross-kind ranking. The grouped arrays answer what a query found among peoples, or among countries; this answers what it found, best first, whatever the kind.

kind.description: Which array of this same response carries the full record for this id.

name.description: The hit's display name in the requested locale, with French fallback — the question stem for a quiz row.

normalizedScore.description: Cross-kind ranking score on [0,1] (migration 069). The match class picks a disjoint band and the kind's own raw relevance is placed inside it, so the class always dominates and the raw magnitude — measured on a different scale per kind — only breaks ties within one class.

snippet.description: Match excerpt where the kind provides one; matched terms are wrapped in [[ ]].

fieldPath.description: Path in the fiche's counted content fields.

text.description: Text value of that field in the fiche.

recordedIn.description: Optional field paths and their text where the fiche records the query as a whole word. Names, lists and prose count; sources[].notes does not.

SearchCompanionSubject.description: One typed subject used to resolve companion content. The identifier must match its type: PPL_* for people, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 for countries, FLG_* for language families, ISO 639-3 lowercase for languages, and PAT_* for patronymes.

SearchCompanionWordMatch.description: A short found by the word the reader typed, not by an entity: there is no subject to name, so the match carries the word itself, lowercased and without accents.

SearchCompanionMatch.description: Why this individual item is related to the requested subjects. Provenance is item-level because different shelves and items may come from different widening rings.

sourceKind.description: What kind of work the source is. Absent when the source records none.

count.description: Total matching items before the response limit is applied.
Total matching items before the response limit is applied.
Total matching items before the response limit is applied.
Total matching quiz items before the single-item response limit is applied.

PeopleSummaryV2.description: Lightweight people reference embedded in a name record.

NameRecordV2.description: A single name-variant record (endonym | exonym | historical_spelling | surname).

ComparisonEntity.description: One compared entity. Section keys are the strict-model content keys for its type; a section absent from the source fiche is an explicit `null`, never omitted.

id.description: PPL_*, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, or FLG_* id

additionalProperties.description: Comparable section value (nullable), keyed by content section name (e.g. appellations, origins, culture).

NameHistorySourceV2.description: A source of a name-history account. An oral source is never refused for having no URL or no page (REQ-195): it names what it can of its narrative, carrier and place.

NameHistoryAccountV2.description: One dated account of a name. Accounts sharing a hypothesisGroup are competing hypotheses, shown side by side and never ranked.

period.description: Integer years, negative before the common era; either bound may be unknown. `label` is what the reader reads.

era.description: The great era of the territory the account is about, at its period: before colonial rule, under it, or since independence. Absent when the account does not settle where or when.

aspect.description: What the account says of the name as a whole: its meaning, who imposed it and why that is a problem, or how it is used today.

formAsWritten.description: A written trace of the name: the form exactly as the cited document spells it, cited at its page.

birth.description: The earliest origin of this name the project knows; at most one per name.

actors.description: Context for the reader, never the author of a name.

WordSearchHitV2.description: A word search hit (REQ-196): exact name match, then a prefix match on any of its names, then a pg_trgm fallback; normalizedScore is the cross-kind scale of migration 069.

WordSummaryV2.description: One row of the word list (REQ-196).

WordV2.description: A word fiche (REQ-196): a word whose history explains Africa through its names. `names` lists every name the word answers to — its filed name, then each nameText of its nameHistory — with no form promoted over another; `nameHistory`, always present for a word, tells where each comes from.

wordLanguage.description: ISO 639-3 code of the language of the word.

definition.description: One sentence: what the word means today.

relatedSubjects.description: Fiches of any class the word is tied to, with the fiche's own sentence saying how.

NameHistoryV2.description: The subject's name history (REQ-196, ARCH-028): one shape on every subject, validated by the one shared schema before it is loaded. Absent when the fiche declares none yet.

selfNameUnknown.description: No source gives the name the people uses for itself; no name is then self-given.

shortLine.description: One sentence a reader understands without context.

usedIn.description: ISO 639-3 codes of the languages the name is used in.

periodLabel.description: When the name is or was in use.

variantSpelling.description: Another spelling of a name rather than a name of its own.

nameEn.description: English name of ordinary use, in the state's own English form (Chad, Côte d'Ivoire, Cabo Verde, The Gambia). Absent until the next data reload fills migration 084's column.

PersonPeopleLinkV2.description: A person's typed link to a people (migration 057, REQ-126): membership (belongs to the people) or observation (studied the people — e.g. an ethnographer). Never inferred — always the value the fiche declares.

PersonSearchResultV2.description: A named person search hit (ARCH-018, REQ-126) — an ethnographer, author, informant, translator, historian, etc.

normalizedScore.description: Cross-kind ranking score on [0,1] (migration 069), the magnitude `results` sorts on.

snippet.description: Match excerpt over fullName and roleCategory; matched terms are wrapped in [[ ]].

peopleLinks.description: This person's typed links to studied/belonged-to peoples — never collapsed into membership.

PatronymeSearchResultV2.description: A name (patronyme) search hit (REQ-135), ranked by afrik_search_patronymes (migration 066): exact name match, then a prefix/accent-insensitive lexical match, then a dmetaphone phonetic match (bridging spellings like Keyta/Keïta), then a pg_trgm typo-tolerance fallback. A name reached only through its phonetic key is offered only when nothing answers the query exactly (migration 108, REQ-201).

associatedPeoples.description: Associated peoples whose fiche exists, resolved to their main name in fiche order — ETNI-1859. Absent when the name declares no people.

normalizedScore.description: Cross-kind ranking score on [0,1] (migration 069), the magnitude `results` sorts on.

snippet.description: Match excerpt over nameMain; matched terms are wrapped in [[ ]].

LanguageSearchResultV2.description: A language search hit (REQ-136), ranked by afrik_search_languages (migration 068): exact match on the ISO 639-3 id or the accent/case-insensitive name, then a prefix/accent-insensitive lexical match over the weighted search_vector (migration 055) OR name_unaccent_vector (this migration).

nameEn.description: The fiche's English name (content.nameEn), carried as fiche data and not searched; null when the fiche carries none.

exactMatch.description: Fires on the ISO 639-3 id as well as on the name — a reader who types "swa" has named the language exactly as precisely as one who types "Swahili".

snippet.description: Match excerpt over name; matched terms are wrapped in [[ ]].

peopleCount.description: Number of afrik_peoples rows carrying this family's id, computed from stored rows (REQ-108) — not the fiche-declared associatedPeoples length.

associatedPeoples.description: Canonical associated peoples derived from afrik_peoples.language_family_id.

content.description: Evolutionary JSONB content. Its associatedPeoples property is a legacy compatibility copy derived from the canonical top-level array.

PatronymeV2.description: A name (patronyme) — DEC-038's fifth dimension of the atlas. Bearer entries are a narrow allow-listed summary; no code path takes a family name and returns an ethnic origin for a named living person (DEC-040).

content.description: Opaque passthrough of the name's remaining DEC-039 fields, forwarded as-is pending ETNI-1460's strict per-subtype shape.

bearers.description: Narrow allow-listed summary — id, fullName, roleCategory only (DEC-040).

namedBearers.description: Bearers the atlas can only name, because no person record exists for them — they carry a name and a status, never an id, a role or a biography, which is why they are a separate list and not a `bearers` entry with empty fields. Only a bearer the atlas records as dead is served: a family name is an ethnic marker, so publishing a living one would publish their ethnic origin (DEC-040, RGPD art. 9).

alliances.description: Names this name is allied with (joking-kinship pacts such as sanankuya), in the dossier's own order. The target is resolved to its name so a client never has to print a raw PAT_ id; allianceType is the attested term, or null when the dossier records the pact without naming it.

ApiResponseMeta.description: Envelope meta block for Module #0 responses. Always carries license + attribution (AR8). Optionally includes pagination, confidence score, and pinned-version URL.

translation.description: No longer emitted: translation of the fiches was retired and every record is served as authored, in French. Kept declared so existing clients are not broken.

TranslationProvenance.description: How the served record was translated (REQ-142). A separate axis from source tier and source_kind; never alters the confidence score.

stale.description: The authored text changed on a served field since the translation was produced.

ApiErrorEntry.description: Error taxonomy entry returned inside the envelope `errors[]` array.

field.description: Field path that triggered the error (validation only)

ApiErrorEnvelope.description: Envelope returned on any non-2xx Module #0 response.

PatronymeLinkV2.description: A name as a fiche lists it — enough to name it and to link to its dossier.

viaPeoples.description: The peoples of this country that bear the name. They are what makes the entry reach rather than attestation, and what lets a reader audit the inference.

CountryPatronymesV2.description: The two name routes a country answers along, kept apart. They assert different things and neither contains the other — measured on the published fiches, 2 countries are reachable only directly and 6 only through their peoples. Summing them publishes an inference under the heading of a sourced fact.

attested.description: Names a source attests in this country (afrik_patronyme_countries).

borneByPeoples.description: Names borne by this country's peoples that are not attested here. The reader is told where the bearers live, not where the name is recorded.

patronymes.description: The names this people bears. Distinct from the ethnonym dossier at /peoples/{id}/names, which holds what the people is called. An empty array is the ordinary state of the fiches, not an omission.

DossierReadingV2.description: One reading of the chapter's subject. Comparative readings are optional; when present, both stances are published.

sourceRefs.description: Keys into the dossier's own sources array.

illustration.description: Credits for the chapter's document. Where the licence requires attribution, author and licenceUrl are both present.

key.description: Raw API key, shown only once.

Source.description: Canonical bibliographic entry. Structured fields are nullable only during the lossless legacy-citation compatibility boundary.

sourceKey.description: Stable source key. Null only for legacy entries awaiting review.

tier.description: Authority the source carries. Null means the citation has not been tiered yet.

identifiers.description: Bibliographic or archival identifiers such as ISBN, DOI, catalogue, or call number.

pinnedUrl.description: Always null: no column backs this field. Kept because removing a published property is a breaking change, and null before reads the same as absent after.

resolvable.description: Always null: the nightly link check writes a log file, not a column. Kept for the same reason as pinnedUrl.

lastVerifiedAt.description: When a human last verified the source. Read from `verified_at`.

notes.description: Why the source carries the tier it carries — the catalogue entry, domain rule, or citation form the tier was read from.

page.description: Locator inside the work, when the citation named one.

ReferenceSource.description: Structured bibliographic reference returned by the contributor reference library.

created.description: True when a new source was created; false when an existing matching source was returned.

ReferenceWorkingAssetCreateInput.description: Multipart private working-asset upload. The submitted file is write-only and never returned by this API.

file.description: Private scan or OCR asset to store.

PrivateReferenceWorkingAsset.description: Metadata for a private working asset. Responses intentionally omit binary content, bucket identifiers, and storage object or location paths; this endpoint does not grant asset retrieval access.

rightsStatus.description: The asset remains private to the working library.

OralNarrative.description: A public, rights-cleared oral narrative, reviewed or not yet reviewed (reviewed narratives are listed first). This representation intentionally excludes transcripts, media locators, collector details, carrier references, reviewer identity, and withheld narrator names.

reviewed.description: Whether the narrative has been reviewed. An unreviewed narrative is shown labelled as not yet reviewed.

Media.description: A media credit (author, licence URI, source page) attached to a fiche. Carries no binary media content or image URL — matching an actual image to a fiche is a separate, manually-curated step (ETNI-1412).

ConfidenceRecord.description: Pre-computed confidence record for a Module #1 fiche. Populated by the `recompute_confidence(entity_type, entity_id)` Postgres function.

ProvenanceCensus.description: How many of a fiche's assertions rest on each source standing, each assertion counted once under the standing of its strongest source. Deliberately not a score: an aggregate over chapters of unequal provenance describes none of them, so no field here averages anything. `assertionCount` is always the sum of the four standings; an assertion citing no source is excluded rather than given a bucket.

standings.description: One count per value of the published source scale. `needs_review` is a transitional marker, not a fourth tier, and it also covers a source row the database left untiered.

ColonialOrigin.description: Present only once the colonial-borders dataset (Story 13.3) documents the pair (NFR31 — additive, optional).

assertionId.description: Backing assertion id, null when no per-field assertion exists yet for this fiche (bulk-migrated data predates the contribution workflow).

PeopleFragmentation.description: Derived strictly from afrik_people_countries + content.demography.distributionByCountry — no data foundation of its own (Epic 13).

selfAppellation.description: The name the people gives itself (content.appellations.selfAppellation), verbatim. Omitted when the fiche records none.

SourcedRelationItem.description: Sourced (never derived) relation, from the perspective of the ego people (Story 11.7).

DerivedRelationItem.description: Read-time-computed linguistic link (FR73) — structurally distinct from a sourced relation, never a flag on a shared shape.

sourceKind.description: What kind of work the source is (provenance, orthogonal to tier). Null or absent when none is recorded.

RelationRecord.description: Non-ego-centered relation record — both sides exposed directly (peopleIdA/peopleIdB) rather than as a single neighbor (Story 11.7).

GeoJSONGeometry.description: Schematic (corridor-level) GeoJSON geometry — never a claim of precise historical borders.

coordinates.description: Nesting depth depends on `type` ([lon, lat] pairs for LineString; arrays thereof for MultiLineString/Polygon).

startYear.description: Astronomical year integer; negative values are BCE.

sourceKind.description: What kind of work the source is (provenance, orthogonal to tier). Null or absent when none is recorded.

MigrationEventSummary.description: List-view migration event — no geometry (AR18 payload-size discipline).

MigrationEventDetail.description: Detail-view migration event, incl. geometry, narrative, peoples and sources.

NameRecordImposition.description: Imposed-name context. Present whenever any of its four fields carries data — including contemporaryUsage on non-imposed endonyms (the illustrative dossier shape), so this is not gated on imposedBy alone.

NameRecord.description: One name entry in a people's names dossier (endonym, exonym, historical spelling, or surname), with per-record sources and the people's confidence score (AR17 batched, not per-record queries).

attestations.description: The form's history (REQ-189): every time it was written down, by whom, with the source at a printed page. Empty when no attestation is recorded.

shortLine.description: One sentence a reader understands without context (REQ-191), at most 120 characters.

namedBy.description: Who gave the form: a people or an authority, never an author. Null for a self-name.

NamePronunciation.description: How the self-name is said (REQ-191): a respelling in the site's language, an optional recording with the speaker's consent, and its source.

FamilyTreeSkeletonFamily.description: Lightweight family header for the tree skeleton. Deliberately omits the full editorial `content` JSONB (see LanguageFamilyV2) to keep the skeleton payload small (ETNI-463 AC3: ≤ 15 KB for the largest family).

LanguageFamilyTree.description: Classification tree skeleton: the family's languages (branches) with linked-people counts, plus peoples in the family not linked to any of its languages.

branchProvenance.description: Which source produced `branches`: the language fiches, or a reconstruction from the ISO codes the people fiches declare. `afrik_languages` now holds 748 rows in recette, but coverage still varies by family, so `people-fiches` remains a common fallback.

declaredBranches.description: Branch names the family fiche states in `generalInfo.branches`. No field ties a people to one of them, so they are a declared register rather than parents in the tree.

PeopleRevisionItem.description: A single published revision in the people revision history list.

moderator_pseudonym.description: Privacy-preserving pseudonym derived from the moderator's internal id

pinned_url.description: Stable URL for this pinned version (AR14). Cache-Control: s-maxage=31536000, immutable.

next_cursor.description: Version to pass as ?cursor= on the next request. Null when no more pages.

PeopleRevisionListResponse.description: Cursor-paginated list of published revisions ordered by version DESC.

PeopleVersionSnapshotResponse.description: Full published snapshot at a pinned version. Data is read from the immutable revision record, never from the live entity (AR14). Response is permanently cacheable (AR18).

data.description: Full denormalised entity state as stored at publication time (snapshot_jsonb)

DoctrineEntry.description: Editorial-doctrine row (MDX source stored in DB).

FeedRevisionItem.description: A single published revision entry in the cross-entity revisions feed.

entity_id.description: Stable entity identifier (PPL_*, FLG_*, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3)

summary.description: Editorial reason for the revision, if provided

FeedCursorPaginationMeta.description: Cursor-based pagination meta for the revisions feed.

next_cursor.description: Opaque base64url cursor. Pass as ?cursor= on the next request. Null when no more pages.

FeedRevisionListResponse.description: Cursor-paginated list of published revisions across all entity types (JSON format).

target_type.description: AFRIK entity type (people, country, language, language_family)

target_id.description: Stable AFRIK identifier of the entity being flagged

target_field_path.description: Optional dotted path to the disputed field

reason_text.example: Population figure appears outdated vs. 2024 census.

reporter_email.description: Optional reply address. The report is created and published whether or not it is supplied. A single-use link is e-mailed to confirm the address, and only a confirmed address ever receives the moderation decision. Never published, and never returned by any endpoint.

language.description: Locale used for reporter verification and moderation-decision e-mails. French is the only one published; missing or other values fail closed to French.

proposed_rewrite.example: Update the population figure using the 2024 census.

antibot.description: A solved proof-of-work challenge, obtained from GET /v2/antibot/challenge. Single-use and short-lived. Nothing in it identifies the caller.

elapsedMs.description: Milliseconds the form was open before submission. A submission faster than a person could have written it is refused.

example.reason_text: Population figure appears outdated compared with the latest census.
example.proposed_rewrite: Update the population figure using the 2024 census.

reason_text.example: Population figure appears outdated compared with the latest census.

proposed_rewrite.example: Update the population figure using the 2024 census.

moderator_notes.description: The moderator's answer on a decided report. Required by the moderation charter on accepted, rejected and duplicate.

remediation_state.description: What changed in the published fiches, separately from what the moderators thought of the report. Written by the publication of a correction, never by a moderator decision. NULL while the report is open or under review.

remediation_published_at.description: When the correction reached the published fiches. Never null when remediation_state is published.

remediation_summary.description: One reader-facing sentence naming what changed, shown verbatim on the public report page.

example.reason_text: Population figure appears outdated compared with the latest census.
example.proposed_rewrite: Update the population figure using the 2024 census.

FlagCursorPaginationMeta.description: Opaque cursor pagination for the public flags list.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor to pass unchanged as ?cursor=. Null when no more pages remain.

FlagAuditEntry.description: One recorded step in a report's life. It names the role that acted and the level it was authorised at, never the person: a register has to establish that a decision was taken and at what level of authorisation, and a public register backed by an internal console has no reason to go further.

occurredAt.description: When the step was recorded. The console renders it in UTC, so a moderation timeline reads the same from every time zone.

authorisationLevel.description: The level the actor held, or null for a reader. The moderation allowlist is flat, so `admin` is the only level the console grants.

entries.description: Oldest first. The first entry is the report's arrival, credited to a reader.

QuizScopeOption.description: One track a session can be drawn from. `playable` is false when the track cannot fill a session of eight — it is still listed, and still counted, rather than hidden.

playableThemeIds.description: The themes this track can fill a session of, in the picker's order. A theme absent from the list cannot be crossed with this track — `?pays=GHA&theme=…` naming an omitted theme answers 422.

QuizThemeOption.description: One domain of content a session can be narrowed to, counted across all the published fiches.

QuizScope.description: The track the returned session was drawn from.

QuizSourceRef.description: The single highest-tier resolvable source backing the question's assertion (official or referenced, FR65 gate).

sourceKind.description: What kind of work the source is. Absent or null when the source records none.

QuizEntityLink.description: The AFRIK entity the question's field value is drawn from.

QuizOptionValue.description: A plain string for non-name fields, or a structured autonym/exonym name.

QuizSessionQuestion.description: One session question. The answer key ships in the payload (correctOption, explanationFr, source) — reveal is client-side.

templateId.description: T1-T4 ask about an atomic fiche field; T6-T11 quote a prose rubric of a people and ask which people it belongs to; T12 asks which of a people's exonyms is contested; T13-T18 do the same over countries. Kept in step with QUIZ_TEMPLATE_IDS by openapiV2 contract tests — the enum had gone stale twice.

stimulusFr.description: Verbatim fiche prose shown above the stem, on the templates whose answer is the subject. Null elsewhere.

QuizSessionData.description: GET /v2/quiz/session result data. Questions arrive in the order they are meant to be played: ascending difficulty band, except under `mode=aleatoire`.

ApiKeySummary.description: One of the caller's own API keys. Never carries the raw key or its hash.

ApiKeyCreated.description: Response to a successful key creation. `key` is the raw key — shown only in this response, never retrievable again.

PlaceSummaryV2.description: One row of the place list (REQ-196).

countryId.description: The place's country when it lies in one; null for a region that spans several (read countryIds).

countryIds.description: Every country the place lies in, in the fiche's order: one for a town, several for a region such as the Sahara.

PlaceV2.description: A place fiche (REQ-196). `names` lists every name the place answers to — its filed name, then each nameText of its nameHistory — with no form promoted over another; `nameHistory` tells where each comes from.

country.description: The place's country when it lies in one; null for a region that spans several (read countries).

countries.description: Every country the place lies in, in the fiche's order: one for a town, several for a region such as the Sahara.

PlaceSearchHitV2.description: A place search hit (REQ-196): exact name match, then a prefix match on any of its names, then a pg_trgm fallback; normalizedScore is the cross-kind scale of migration 069.

countryId.description: The place's country when it lies in one; null for a region that spans several (read countryIds).
